TMS motor-evoked potentials with PhysioNeurophys

Source: vignettes/PhysioNeurophys.Rmd
PhysioNeurophys.Rmd

PhysioNeurophys analyses transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and peripheral motor neurophysiology on PhysioExperiment objects: motor-evoked-potential (MEP) amplitude and latency, Boltzmann recruitment curves, H-reflex and F-wave metrics, paired-pulse SICI/ICF, cortical silent period, TMS-EEG cleaning, and the PREP2 prognosis algorithm.

This vignette uses the built-in simulator so it runs offline. TEP/MEP labels are measurement windows, not proof of a cortical source.

library(PhysioNeurophys)
#> Loading required package: PhysioExperiment

1. Simulate epoched MEPs

make_mep() generates biphasic MEP waveforms with a known latency and a Boltzmann amplitude-intensity relationship, and attaches the per-trial TMS pulse metadata. Epochs start 20 ms before the pulse.

pe <- make_mep(n_trials = 12, seed = 1)
dim(SummarizedExperiment::assay(pe))   # samples x channels x trials
#> [1] 600   1  12
getTMSpulses(pe)[1:3, ]
#>   pulse intensity_pct_mso target coil rmt_pct_mso onset_sec
#> 1     1          30.00000   <NA> <NA>          NA        NA
#> 2     2          33.63636   <NA> <NA>          NA        NA
#> 3     3          37.27273   <NA> <NA>          NA        NA

2. MEP amplitude

Peak-to-peak amplitude is measured within a response window, per channel and trial. Pass epoch_start_ms = -20 to match the simulated epoch.

amp <- mepAmplitude(pe, epoch_start_ms = -20)
head(amp[, c("trial", "intensity_pct_mso", "p2p")])
#>   trial intensity_pct_mso       p2p
#> 1     1          30.00000 0.1306161
#> 2     2          33.63636 0.1487786
#> 3     3          37.27273 0.2217329
#> 4     4          40.90909 0.3351076
#> 5     5          44.54545 0.5334475
#> 6     6          48.18182 0.8296879

3. MEP onset latency 

lat <- mepLatency(pe, epoch_start_ms = -20)
head(lat[, c("trial", "onset_sample", "latency_ms")])
#>   trial onset_sample latency_ms
#> 1     1           NA         NA
#> 2     2           NA         NA
#> 3     3           NA         NA
#> 4     4          206       21.0
#> 5     5          204       20.6
#> 6     6          203       20.4

4. Boltzmann recruitment curve

Amplitude rises sigmoidally with stimulator intensity. recruitmentCurve() fits a three-parameter logistic and returns the fitted parameters and fit quality.

rc <- recruitmentCurve(pe, epoch_start_ms = -20)
rc
#> MEP recruitment curve
#>   MEP_max: 2.0731
#>   S50: 50.097 %MSO
#>   k: 5.6192 %MSO
#>   Maximum slope: 0.092231
#>   R-squared: 0.99778
#>   Trials: 12; converged: TRUE

Where to go next

?PhysioNeurophys lists every entry point, including peripheral measures (hReflexRecruitment(), hMaxMMax(), fWaveDetect()), paired-pulse inhibition/facilitation (pairedPulse(), siciIcf()), the cortical silent period (corticalSilentPeriod()), TMS-EEG pulse removal and cleaning (removeTMSpulse(), tmsSSPSIR(), soundClean(), tepAverage()), and the PREP2 upper-limb prognosis (prep2()).
